entry_points.text: Listing requires zeroed flags, caps count at one million, checks caller buffer, copies a request and selects scoped or global enumeration.
Destroy is terminal teardown while drain is reentrant via drainer counting and loops until all pool queues test empty.
Multithread accepts arbitrary size and thread limits; mask set and hotplug callbacks drive lifecycle with valid role selection required.
Early startup registers hotplug handling and links per-CPU descriptors into a global free pool with warning-only failure; generic show and store adapt object ops to instance behavior.

exports.text: Parallel submit validates shell, assigns order, queues work or runs inline when pool empty; serial stages finished jobs per CPU and dispatches contiguous runs.
Targeted queueing is at-most-once pending; attribute replace runs serialized for unbound queues; attribute free tolerates null.
Destroy drains, stops rescue, verifies empty and releases refs; drain loops to global empty; flush waits prior items; diagnostics print only active queues.
Multithread splits a range over helpers plus caller and waits, with empty and single-helper fast paths; mask set selects role, rejecting unknown roles.
Instance create builds helpers and affinity, failing cleanly; release drops embedded ref; shell attach and detach run protected, tolerating null on free.
Scan splits text into name/value pairs; dash equals underscore in names; uint setter enforces numeric form and min/max; scalar family publishes setter, getter, ops.

hazards.text: Enumeration drops read-side guard to copy each identifier out, pinning the validated item across the copy with ref handling on fault before re-entering.
Teardown refuses workers with active, scheduled or non-idle state and clears cached wake refs; empty work pool at submit runs the function synchronously to preserve progress.

Create failures unwind identity and memory without attach, interrupted thread create distinct; double idle, bad hash linkage and running-while-all-idle warn; busy destroy warns, dumps and aborts; drain warns when stalled; parallel-data build unwinds in order, replace halts yet waits and releases predecessors, invalid masks stop, freeing with shells warns.

Offline drain warns and returns; full color ring parks newcomers on overflow with only leader cascading after protected recheck; verbose dumps run masked with deferred console and watchdog refresh; mask store discards scratch on failure; arg handling reports setters re-enabling interrupts; unregister clears cached pointer first, tolerates absence, with a no-op build.

invariants.text: Lookup lower-bounds a per-type or unified index under a reader guard, returning live refs only for active objects; traversal gives first, next, end; listing resumes after a predecessor with single-type filter when one bit set.

Submission assigns increasing labels under exclusion and normalizes placement with deterministic fallback; serial dispatch advances label and CPU with wrap reset; per-CPU staging stays sorted by wrap-aware order.

Effective CPUs intersect request with allowed unbound set, falling back to full allowed set when disjoint; pool-queue build reuses or creates a pool and unwinds on failure; queueing fires only on non-pending to pending change.

Multithread start preallocates helpers for all but caller and chains them, stopping when pool empties; bulk release returns a chain under protection tolerating empty; restriction applies a temp mask then releases it.

Bring-up reserves identity, allocates on pool node, names thread by rescue, per-CPU or unbound case, binds priority and CPU, attaches under guard; idle entry pushes LIFO and arms timer on surplus; surplus counts an active manager as idle.

Clearing sets terminal scope, non-ordered mode, broadened mask under strictness; hash and equality always use priority, strictness, pod mask plus general mask only when non-strict; pod mask intersects pod with wanted CPUs with fallback; commit publishes slots.

Pool starts with sentinel identity and CPU, disassociated state, empty lists, deferrable idle timer with cull work, mayday timer, single ref, cleared attrs; pool-queue requires alignment, negative flush color, single ref, and a cursor that never runs as work.

Helpers claim aligned chunks under guard, run caller code unlocked, signal on last finisher; helper count derives from size over max of minimum and alignment clamped to caller max; chunk size uses a load factor, lower bound and alignment, optional NUMA round-robin.

Reorder and serial areas init per CPU in parallel and callback sets; parallel data intersects masks with online CPUs minus offlining CPU, sequence negative one, ref one; start and stop toggle init with grace wait; replace publishes per shell with reset and reverse release; hotplug acts only for members.

Emptiness means zero active with empty inactive list; colors advance modulo a fixed ring; busy covers in-flight colors, extra refs or non-empty; prep marks only participants in the color, optionally advances color, completes at once when none wait.

Sysfs handlers recover instance and entry and invoke callbacks only when present; mask show and store select serial or parallel by name; defaults are the two mask entries plus terminator; object type binds dispatch with default groups and freeing release.

Lookup enforces level bounds, rejects missing values unless arg-free use is declared, delegates unknown names; locked-down hardware params refuse while unsafe ones taint and warn yet proceed; value allocs track globally and free only on exact pointer match.

Diagnostics collapse repeats of one work function into counted form and show barriers by owner; pool lines report affinity, node, flags, priority with distinct bottom-half form; worker lines add rescue marking.

locks.text: A dedicated global spin guard protects reusable work-pool membership on alloc and free, bottom-half-safe on submit with explicit bottom-half handling on workers.

Each per-CPU reorder collection and serial queue has its own lock; reorder mutates under the reorder lock, serial append and wake hold the serial lock with callbacks after release; shell reads use short read-side guard plus shared-state refs.

Global pool mutex serializes attr prep, pool get and teardown; per-pool interrupt-masked spin guards queue refs, counts, idle moves and wakeups; attach mutex stabilizes disassociated status across attach and detach.

Queue mutex guards colors, waiters, commit, link and destroy or drain state, released across sleeps; pool spin guards per-pool color moves and diagnostic checks; slot and parallel-data publish use read-copy-update with grace waits before free.

Chunk claiming holds a spin guard only across interval and counter updates; mask and hotplug hold the instance mutex with processor read guard across updates; param mutation uses a global or module mutex while a spin guard protects the tracked alloc list.

state_machines.text: Job moves from submit with shared ref through parallel run, ordered staging, serial queueing and callback, ending in batched release that frees masks and per-CPU areas on final drop.

Attr change moves from validation and prep through commit to cleanup, ordered queues pausing until drain, prep failure releasing partial state; unbound pools move from lookup or node-aware create with identity and first worker through reuse to unhash, quiesce, retire idlers, cancel timers, defer reclaim.

Worker flags move prepared to idle with unbound marking for disassociated pools; pool and queue flags separate bottom-half, disassociated, destroying, draining, bound; destroying is set once before draining, draining tracks drainers; instance flags separate init, reset, invalid with stop-before-replace and conditional restart.

Drain moves assign to sleep to cascade where leader wakes peers, advances finished marker, folds overflow and promotes next leader; create unwinds helpers and masks in reverse on failure; arg scan skips space, ends at bare terminator preserving errors, else records and continues.

structs.text: Work wrapper pairs a schedulable element with free-pool linkage and payload; on-stack indicator value one selects on-stack init; job control pairs exclusion with completion, job link, tallies and chunk size; file scope anchors storage with a lock.

Worker carries identity, thread, pool, idle, busy, scheduled and member links, flags, stamp, rescue link; pool carries lock, identity, CPU, node, flags, stamp, lists, index, timers with cull work, workers, allocator, hash, ref, attrs, counts; init uses negative identity and CPU, no node, disassociated, ref one, deferrable timer, idle threshold two.

Attrs carry priority, scope, strictness, ordered mark, general and pod masks; pool queue carries pool and parent links, colors, ref, inactive list, pending, collection and mayday links, release and cursor embedding queue address with pending, associated and inactive marks; parent carries mutex, flags, drainers, attrs, color, slots; negative one means no color.

Job describes start, size, min chunk, alignment, thread cap, NUMA hint, function, arg; shared state has job, chunk size, counts, lock, completion; parallel data has shell, per-CPU areas, masks, sequence, ref, current CPU; instance has masks, validation mask, shells, flags, lock, hotplug link, queues; sequence negative one, ref one, load factor four, unknown role invalid.

Sysfs entry embeds an attribute with optional show and store; tracked param node links globally with trailing value bytes; flush waiter pairs queue link with color and completion; coalescing keeps repeat count with pending function; masks are serial_cpumask and parallel_cpumask, writable 0644 and read-only 0400, applied via serial or parallel selectors.
